rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an actor invites several external parties to submit offers and then states that the same actor selects one of them: Model the invitation as a send task directed to the external parties' pool, then add a user task for the selection, performed by the same actor, connected after it by a sequence flow. Connect that selection task to the next step of the process, so the choice of one offer is not skipped.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an actor invites several external parties to submit offers and then states that the same actor selects one of them

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists two or more follow-up activities that are each performed only under a stated condition (such as 'if necessary') and may occur together or alone, and then continues with a step that must wait for whichever of them were performed: Model an inclusive gateway that splits into a conditional flow to each optional activity, with the condition taken from the description, and a matching inclusive gateway that joins those flows before the next step. Do not use an exclusive gateway, because more than one branch may run, and do not use a parallel gateway, because not every branch is required.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists two or more follow-up activities that are each performed only under a stated condition (such as 'if necessary') and may occur together or alone, and then continues with a step that must wait for whichever of them were performed

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names several distinct roles or departments, each of which performs its own activities within the same process, and it does not state that they are independent communicating participants

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person invites several outside providers to submit offers, then selects one of them, and the selected provider is then engaged for the work as a further described action before the next decision: Model the invitation of the providers as a send task, then the person's selection of one offer as a user task. Add a separate task after the selection for the described action that engages the chosen provider (for example, confirming or placing the order), and do not let the flow go directly from the selection to the next gateway. Connect these tasks by sequence flows in the order the description gives: invitation to selection, selection to engagement, and engagement to the following gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person invites several outside providers to submit offers, then selects one of them, and the selected provider is then engaged for the work as a further described action before the next decision

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a conditional case in which one participant invites several external parties to make offers and then selects one of them, and the branch then continues to a later decision: Model the invitation of external parties as a send task placed in the true branch of the condition. Connect it by a sequence flow to a separate task in which the same participant selects one offer. Connect that selection task to the later decision gateway. Do not connect the invitation or any other step of the true branch, or any alternative branch, directly to the later decision gateway, and do not omit the selection task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a conditional case in which one participant invites several external parties to make offers and then selects one of them, and the branch then continues to a later decision

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an actor sends requests to several external parties asking for proposals, and then, in a separate step, says that the actor selects one of those parties, so the selection depends on the proposals received: Model the selection as its own bpmn:task, labeled with the selection action the description names, placed on the sequence flow after the task that sends the requests and before any gateway or activity that depends on the selection. Do not merge the selection into the request task and do not omit it, even when the description states the selection in a separate sentence or treats it as a consequence of the requests.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an actor sends requests to several external parties asking for proposals, and then, in a separate step, says that the actor selects one of those parties, so the selection depends on the proposals received

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an actor asks several outside parties for offers and then selects one of them, and it does not describe those outside parties as doing anything in the process after they give their offers: Model the request to the outside parties as one send task in the actor's own lane. Do not add a pool for those parties, a message flow to them, or a receiving participant. Model the selection of one offer as one task in the same actor lane, with the next action the description attributes to that selection (for example, placing the order) included in that task when the description states them together. Do not add a separate user task or gateway for the selection.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an actor asks several outside parties for offers and then selects one of them, and it does not describe those outside parties as doing anything in the process after they give their offers
